question: What is the meaning of u-value in relation to building physics?
description: The U-value is a measure of thermal transmittance or heat transfer through a building element, indicating its thermal conductivity. It is expressed in units of W/m²K (Watts per square meter per degree Kelvin) and is inversely related to the R-value, which is the reciprocal of the U-value. A lower U-value signifies better insulation properties and higher thermal resistance, contributing to improved energy efficiency in buildings.
